source_scope: Owned local/imported Windows monitored fences connected to genuine experimental R0 fence callbacks and attached native COPY/COMPUTE/DIRECT queues.
required_sequence: Query private native fence bundle and allocate queried aligned runtime storage
PrepareFence creates or imports an actual KMT mapping on the exact runtime-selected guest LUID
CreateFence validates its genuine R0 descriptor against the owned GPU address
AttachQueue enables bounded logical scheduling for the native queue before admitting additional logical queues
Use genuine SignalFence/WaitForFence and the existing ExecuteCommandLists path
DrainQueue and retry retirement after actual work completion; failures never imply completed signals

limits.host_submission: Existing selected VkQueue accepts one retained native command submission at a time. CPU waits consume no physical queue slot. Other ready waits/signals progress while unrelated host work remains pending.
limits.OS_waits: Actual asynchronous KMT CPU wait events capture intermediate shared values, including rewinds; no blocking future-value wait occurs on submitting threads.

ownership: Every queued list retains its exact generation and recording until actual submission; old cleanup cannot release a reset replacement.
Every signal/wait retains the exact fence and its owned KMT device/mapping. Shared NT handles are borrowed during import; exported handles are owned and closed by the caller.
The worker pins its containing module. Last-queue retirement joins it; failed stop retains the queue and refuses new admissions until retirement retry.
Accepted or uncertain host attempts are never replayed. Pending signals remain uncompleted after execution errors; only proven drain permits cancellation and owner release.
OS teardown failure preserves partially destroyed owners and exact native claims for retry. Hidden failed construction owners are collected before device retirement.
explicit_boundaries: The experimental source requires owned PrepareFence registration; arbitrary runtime GPU VAs outside that mapping are declined. Caller-provided GPU notification threshold addresses are declined; KMT owns threshold notification.
No complete public D3D12 mandatory interface, WDDM context/resource registration, residency, general GPUVA mapping or hardware queue implementation is advertised.
Cross-adapter fence sharing and unbounded scheduling are outside this bounded single-adapter subset.
Actual Windows KMT notification, cross-process/API shared fence execution and native GPU acceptance have not been run; controlled fixtures model KMT/Vulkan services.

runtime_status_without_fences.implementation: The existing removal query first probes the retained native runtime DeviceStatusQuery Escape callback, then preserves its existing retained-KMT-fence observation path. Existing queue/fence pumps also sample runtime contexts with no fence.
runtime_status_without_fences.ownership: The actual runtime device and parent generation stay pinned across the outside-lock callback. Recursive status calls return the last known state and cannot enter another Escape. Confirmed loss is sticky and no fence progress is invented.
runtime_status_without_fences.qualification: Modeled Windows ABI regression only; public ID3D12Device/ID3D12Fence integration remains unavailable.
